source: NCERT-aligned UPSC Ecology & Environment (Class XI), Ch. 11 (Forests, Agriculture and Environmental Issues).

sections.heading: 1. Forests and Deforestation
points: Forests provide **timber, fuel, fodder, medicines, biodiversity, carbon storage, and climate/soil/water regulation**.
**Deforestation** — clearing of forests for agriculture, mining, dams, urbanisation; causes soil erosion, loss of biodiversity, floods, and climate change.
**Afforestation and social forestry** aim to restore green cover; the desired forest cover is **33%**.

sections.heading: 2. Forest Conservation Movements and Rights
points: **Chipko Movement (1970s, Uttarakhand)** — villagers hugged trees to prevent felling (Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt).
**Appiko Movement** (Karnataka) — the southern counterpart.
**Joint Forest Management (JFM)** — community participation.
**Forest Rights Act (2006)** — recognises rights of forest-dwelling tribal communities.

sections.heading: 3. Agriculture and the Environment
points: The **Green Revolution** raised output but caused **overuse of water, chemical fertilisers and pesticides** → soil degradation, water pollution (eutrophication), falling water tables.
**Monoculture** reduces agro-biodiversity; **shifting cultivation (jhum)** can degrade land.
**Sustainable agriculture:** **organic farming, integrated pest management, crop rotation, drip irrigation, agroforestry**.
**Genetically Modified (GM) crops** (e.g. Bt cotton) — debated for benefits and risks.

sections.heading: 4. Land Degradation and Desertification
points: **Land degradation** — decline in land quality (erosion, salinity, waterlogging, loss of fertility).
**Desertification** — degradation in arid/semi-arid areas turning land barren; addressed by **UNCCD**.
Causes: deforestation, overgrazing, faulty irrigation, mining.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Desired forest cover = 33%; deforestation causes erosion, floods, biodiversity loss.
Chipko Movement (1970s, Uttarakhand); Appiko (Karnataka).
Forest Rights Act (2006) = rights of forest-dwelling tribals.
Green Revolution's environmental costs: chemical overuse, falling water table, eutrophication.
Sustainable farming: organic, IPM, crop rotation, drip irrigation, agroforestry; UNCCD = desertification.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Chipko Movement** was about **saving forests** (tree-hugging, Uttarakhand).
The **Forest Rights Act (2006)** recognises **tribal/forest-dweller rights**.
The **UNCCD** deals with **desertification** (land degradation in drylands).
The **Green Revolution had environmental costs** (chemical overuse, water depletion).
